newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major widens attack on "inconsistent" Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major widens attack on "inconsistent" Blair.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major will later on Friday attack Labour leader Tony Blair for having constantly changed his political stance on key issues, aides travelling on Major's election battlebus said.

Major began his personal attack on the Labour leader at a morning news conference in London, accusing him of preparing to sell Britain out if he wins the May 1 election and then goes to an EU summit in Amsterdam the following month.
But the aides said Major will widen his offensive against Blair in the speech which is due to be delivered in Manchester at 1700 gmt.

He will point out that in 1983 Blair said he wanted Britain to leave the EU and in 1986 was willing for Britain unilaterally to give up its nuclear deterrent -- positions which are the opposite of those he currently holds.

The aides quoted the text of Major's speech as saying: "Mr Blair changes his mind as often as a grasshopper jumps...why should we trust a word Labour say when they don't stand by a word they said 10, five, or three minutes ago." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
